body:
Nothing for you to do. You never need to type in chat: a session the kit launches never attaches a repo. The orchestrator, which holds both repos, runs the real-project check. Messages between sessions are now pointers of at most 200 characters, enforced by a hook. Clearing the 11 merged branches waits for your go: `kit.py branches --delete`.

## Numbers now (at 8b49dfb, merged with main)
- `tests/test_cl38_add_repo.py`: 19 of 19.
- `scripts/run_all_tests.py`: 11 of 11 suites, with `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` unset and full git history. A shallow clone skips 1 of 4 present-runtimes tests, the one O55 saw fail; unshallowed, it runs and passes.
- `kit/test_end_session.py`: 7 of 7.

## O55's second check (o55-cl38-gaps2-0345)
1. `whoami` now prefers a real id: `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` (as `session_<id>`), then `KIT_SESSION_ID`, then `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, then the name given, else an empty string, never a made-up id.
4. `check_trunk_merged`: a fetch that fails or times out now refuses Done. Only a repo with no origin is skipped, and the docstring says so.
5. The numbers are in one place, § Numbers now, and the stale ones are removed.
6. `test_install_present_runtimes.py`: the allowed-hooks list includes `kit_say_it_once.py`. That test was skipped in this shallow clone and runs once unshallowed: 4 of 4.

## O55's gaps (o55-cl38-gaps-0250): all 5 closed
1. **session_id**: the prompt's turn-1 line now runs `kit.py whoami <project>-<part>`. A web part prints `session_<id>` (its `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` `cse_<id>`, the id send_message takes); a CLI part prints the name given. Run here: `session_01AE1HGm4GLpDYDS9nBPA9AN`.
2. **The merged branch** (works on a plain remote; NOT in a web session, whose git proxy refuses branch deletes: end_session now says so): `kit/end_session.py` deletes the part's branch from origin once it is on main (`kit.keep_branches: true` keeps it). It is end_session, not `done`, because `done` runs before the merge and main does not hold the branch yet. `kit/test_end_session.py`: branch deleted, 7 of 7.
3. **The 200 reaches Harmonize**: `--update` now puts the kit's `kit_say_it_once.py` in `.claude/hooks/kit/`. For a project with its own say-it-once hook, it is wired on PreToolUse only (`send_message|SendMessage`); its own hook keeps every other event. The config's `message_chars` and `done_message_chars` above 200 are lowered to 200, and logged. Harmonize copy (/tmp/cl38/r3/hz): limits 600/240 -> 200/200; a 300-character send_message is refused (rc 2); its own `say_it_once.py` hooks are unchanged. The kit repo's own config is lowered too.
4. **An unfetchable trunk**: `done` now refuses ("cannot fetch origin/main"). Only a repo with no origin at all is skipped.
5. Test counts fixed in this body.
Suite and test counts: see § Numbers now.

## Last change (O54's go: o54-no-chat-attach-0215, o54-messages-waste-0218, o54-branches-0225)
- **Parts never attach.** A launched session's classifier refuses `add_repo` whatever the allow rule says, unless you type it. So `kit.py launch` no longer tells a part to attach. Its prompt now says the real-project run is the orchestrator's. `resume` points a part to the Artifact's `kit_docs` for another project's files. `kit.py done` says `real_project` is pending, and no longer refuses a part over it. The review lines say the orchestrator runs it by subagent. `kit/lessons.md` K-line rewritten. `kit.py attach` and the allow rule stay, for a session where you are typing anyway.
- **Messages are pointers.** `kit_say_it_once.py` refuses a message between sessions over 200 characters (whatever `kit.limits` says), or one holding a table, a quote or a code block. Before, the cap was 600 and only `SendMessage` was checked. It now covers both `SendMessage` and `mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message`. The CLI install and this repo's own settings were widened. The clerk's forward of your words is still never cut.
- **Done needs the trunk.** `kit.py done` refuses a branch that lacks `origin/main` ("merge it first"). A part that started on an older kit (CL37 before CL36's rule) is judged by the kit as it is now.
- **No part branches.** `kit.py launch` puts an attached board's prompt on the clone's trunk when the trunk permission is on. Before, it went on `part-<post>`. It falls back to `part-<post>` when the trunk permission is off, or the clone's local trunk has unpushed commits.
- **Sweep.** `kit.py branches` lists origin's branches fully on main; `--delete` removes them in one push. It keeps main, `board-mirror`, `kit-usage`, the current branch, the branch of any post not done, and any branch with work not on main. Run here: 40 branches, 11 fully on main, 13 kept with work not on main. Not deleted: your go.
- Guide: `.kit/BOARD.md` § Attaching another repo on the web (rewritten), § Messages between sessions are pointers, § Branches. The kit repo's own `.kit/kit.py`, `.kit/BOARD.md`, `.kit/lessons.md` and its hook copy are refreshed.
- Tests (last change): `tests/test_cl38_add_repo.py`, 8 tests added here ( pointer passes, over 200 refused, table, quote and code refused, the owner's forward kept, both send tools hooked, Done refuses until the trunk is merged, prompt on the trunk, branches deletes only merged ones). `test_install.py` updated for the widened matcher. Suite counts: see § Numbers now.
- Harmonize, final code, a fresh copy: `install.py --update` adds the allow rule and CL37's usage hooks (Stop, SessionEnd). Its own hooks and rules are kept. Commits: 2fb7407, merged with main at a8fd60f.

## What changed (first change)
- `install.py`: every Claude Code install, new or `--update`, merges `mcp__claude-code-remote__add_repo` into `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow` (`ALLOW_RULES`). It keeps the project's own allow and deny rules, never adds the rule twice, and writes nothing when the rule is already there.
- `kit.py attach <owner/repo>` (new, listed in `kit.py commands`): with no clone yet, it prints the `add_repo` call to make. After that call it clones the repo next to the project (`../<repo>`), records `{name, path, github}` in `.kit/config.json` `portfolio` (once), and prints the `register_repo_root` call. It warns if this project lacks the allow rule.
- `kit.py doctor`: an `add_repo:` line, and an issue when a project with an attached board (portfolio, Artifact board, or the kit repo) lacks the rule.
- Guide: `.kit/BOARD.md` § Attaching another repo on the web (plain steps; only a one-repo session reads `.claude/settings.json`, so start on the repo whose hooks must run; a running session never rereads it; ask the owner when the classifier refuses). The README's web install points to it.

## Harmonize (real project)
- add_repo anlonlt/harmonize (read): refused at turn 1 with the rule in place; allowed after your "attach harmonize"; cloned to /home/user/harmonize at e410d31 and registered. Never pushed.
- `install.py /tmp/cl38/hz --update` on a copy: `.claude/settings.json` +5 lines only (the `permissions.allow` block). The hook counts per event are the same before and after (SessionStart 1, PreToolUse 4, PreCompact 1, Stop 2, UserPromptSubmit 1, PostToolUse 6). A second `--update` changed nothing.

## Tests
- `tests/test_cl38_add_repo.py` (first change): 7 tests (a fresh install and an update keep the project's own allow and deny rules, a pre-CL38 install gets the rule on `--update`, the kit repo has it, the doctor check, attach prints the call, attach records the repo once).
- Suite counts: see § Numbers now.

- A brand-new web session started on Harmonize after its own `install.py --update` is committed: Harmonize's real settings were not changed (never pushed).
- Whether the classifier lets an orchestrator-started session attach a repo with no owner words. Today it did not.

title: Attaching repos on the web: install.py allows add_repo, kit attach, doctor warns
verdict: Installs allow add_repo; kit.py attach and doctor work. Launched parts never attach: the orchestrator runs the real-project check. Messages between sessions are capped at 200 characters. Done needs the trunk merged.
